newsitem.title: USA: Oshman's sees Q4 loss from store closings.
newsitem.headline: Oshman's sees Q4 loss from store closings.

text.p: Oshman's Sporting Goods Inc said Friday it expects to post a restructuring charge of about $11 million in the fourth quarter from the intended closings of about 50 stores, leading it to project a loss in the quarter of between $1.72 and $2.06 per share.
Sales for the quarter ending February 1 are expected to be about $112 million, down from sales of $117.3 million for the same period in the prior year.
The 50 stores are to be closed in the 1997 fiscal year, between February 2 and January 31, 1998.
The expected charge is to cover leasehold and other asset writeoffs, inventory adjustments, employee costs and lease termination costs, it said.
During the 1996 fiscal year, those 50 stores are estimated to contribute about $51 million in sales and to incur direct store losses of about $2.5 million, the company said.

During the 1996 fiscal year, the company already closed 25 stores that contributed $17 million in sales during the year and are expected to incur direct store losses of $2.3 million, including store closing costs, it said.

The company's projected fourth quarter loss of between $10 million and $12 million, or between $1.72 and $2.06 per share, compares with net income in the prior year's fourth quarter of $4.1 million, or $0.67 per share.
Aside from the restructuring charge, the company said the results are primarily attributable to lower than expected sales and increased markdowns during the holiday season.
Oshman's said it also plans to cut costs and take other steps to achieve annual savings of about $3.5 million.
The stores being closed are considered "traditional," smaller stores.
Oshman's said it will now concentrate on its SuperSports USA megastores. It plans to open six more SuperSports in the 1997 fiscal year, it said.
Before the closings, it had 84 "traditional" stores and 31 megastores.
